newsitem.title: MEXICO: Televisa shares rise sharply on new plan.
newsitem.headline: Televisa shares rise sharply on new plan.

text.p: Shares of Mexican media giant Grupo Televisa SA de CV rose sharply early on Wednesday after the announcement of cost-cutting plans by the company.
"We saw this coming for the last few days, and it looks like it should be good for the company," said one stock trader.
The company's CPO rose sharply, and by mid-morning was trading 4.3 percent higher at 105.0 pesos.
In New York, the ADRs rose 1-3/8 to 26-7/8 dollars.
Televisa said it plans to cut costs by $270 million over the next three years and reduce its current total debt level of $988 million by $100 million.
The company said that through a combination of the strengthening Mexican economy, cost cutting measures and efforts to increase revenues, it expected cash flow margins to exceed 25 percent.
